Apple___Apple_scab.title: Apple: Apple Scab 🍏
Apple___Apple_scab.advice: A fungal disease causing dark, olive-green spots on leaves and fruit. Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to prevent spores from overwintering. Apply an approved copper-based fungicide early in the spring at green tip stage.

Apple___Black_rot.title: Apple: Black Rot 🍎
Apple___Black_rot.advice: Causes frogeye leaf spots and cankers on limbs. Prune out dead wood, mummified fruit, and active cankers during winter dormancy. Burn or discard infected cuttings far away from your orchard.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.title: Apple: Cedar Apple Rust 🍂
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.advice: Recognizable by bright orange-yellow spots on the upper leaf surfaces. This fungus requires nearby Juniper/Cedar trees to complete its life cycle. Treat with preventative sulfur or preventative fungicides as blossoms open.

Apple___healthy.title: Apple: Perfectly Healthy! 🍏
Apple___healthy.advice: Great job! Leaves display optimal cellular structure and vigor. Maintain regular structural pruning to improve interior airflow and maximize sunlight penetration.

Blueberry___healthy.title: Blueberry: Perfectly Healthy! 🫐
Blueberry___healthy.advice: Excellent health profile. Ensure your soil pH remains highly acidic (between 4.5 and 5.5) and keep a thick layer of pine bark mulch to conserve vital root moisture.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.title: Cherry: Powdery Mildew 🍒
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.advice: A white, powdery fungal coating choking new shoot growth. Prune lower limbs to increase lower canopy airflow. Apply potassium bicarbonate or neem oil sprays at the very first sign of dynamic white patches.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.title: Cherry: Perfectly Healthy! 🍒
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.advice: Optimal foliar health detected. Keep a steady look out for early spring pests and ensure consistent, deep root irrigation rather than overhead sprinkling.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.title: Corn: Gray Leaf Spot 🌽
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.advice: Presents as distinct blocky, rectangular tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins. Rotate crops next season away from grasses and consider planting disease-resistant hybrid varieties to break the cycle.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.title: Corn: Common Rust 🌽
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.advice: Identified by powdery, reddish-brown pustules rupturing on both sides of the leaf. Rust thrives in high humidity. Avoid overhead irrigation and apply targeted foliar fungicides if infection spikes during early whorl stages.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.title: Corn: Northern Leaf Blight 🌽
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.advice: Characterized by long, cigar-shaped grayish-green lesions on the leaves. Deep-plow old crop residue to bury spores or rotate fields with non-host crops like soybeans for at least one full year.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.title: Corn: Perfectly Healthy! 🌽
Corn_(maize)___healthy.advice: Strong, vibrant leaf nitrogen levels. Keep monitoring for stalk strength and ensure balanced macronutrient fertilization (NPK) to optimize kernel yield.

Grape___Black_rot.title: Grape: Black Rot 🍇
Grape___Black_rot.advice: A destructive fungal attack that shrivels grapes into hard black mummies. Prune away all mummified clusters during winter dormancy. Spray with an organic copper fungicide beginning at early bud break.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).title: Grape: Esca (Black Measles) 🍇
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).advice: Causes striking 'tiger-stripe' yellowing patterns on leaves and dark spots on berries. It enters through large pruning wounds. Protect open wood cuts with specialized pruning sealants during winter maintenance.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.title: Grape: Isariopsis Leaf Blight 🍇
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.advice: Causes irregular dull brown spots on older, lower leaves first. Clear away fallen organic debris from beneath the vines to reduce spore density. Treat canopy with preventative fungicides if conditions stay wet.

Grape___healthy.title: Grape: Perfectly Healthy! 🍇
Grape___healthy.advice: Beautiful foliar integrity. Keep up with strategic canopy thinning to ensure maximum grape cluster exposure to sunlight and wind, which keeps fungal spores from sticking.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).title: Orange: Citrus Greening (HLB) 🍊
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).advice: A severe bacterial infection spread by the Asian citrus psyllid, causing mottled yellow leaves and bitter, misshapen fruit. There is no cure; aggressively manage psyllid insects with neem oil and pull out severely compromised trees to protect adjacent orchards.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.title: Peach: Bacterial Spot 🍑
Peach___Bacterial_spot.advice: Causes water-soaked spots that drop out, leaving a 'shot-hole' appearance in the leaf. Apply a dynamic copper spray program during late dormancy and early spring. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which creates overly tender, vulnerable leaves.

Peach___healthy.title: Peach: Perfectly Healthy! 🍑
Peach___healthy.advice: Excellent fruit-tree vigor. Ensure proper fruit thinning along the branches in early summer to prevent heavy loads from snapping healthy limbs.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.title: Bell Pepper: Bacterial Spot 🫑
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.advice: Small, raised warts appear on the undersides of leaves, leading to severe defoliation. Never work in your garden patch when plants are wet. Apply preventative copper sprays every 7–14 days during periods of warm, rainy weather.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.title: Bell Pepper: Perfectly Healthy! 🫑
Pepper,_bell___healthy.advice: Vibrant, robust growth. Maintain deep, uniform watering at the base of the pepper plants to prevent blossom end rot on developing fruit.

Potato___Early_blight.title: Potato: Early Blight 🥔
Potato___Early_blight.advice: Identified by dark spots with distinctive concentric rings forming a 'target' pattern. Practice strict 3-year crop rotation and maximize soil potassium. Apply preventative organic bio-fungicides early in the summer season.

Potato___Late_blight.title: Potato: Late Blight (Warning!) 🥔
Potato___Late_blight.advice: The highly aggressive pathogen behind historical famines; causes large, water-soaked dark blurs that rot tubers rapidly. Destroy infected plants immediately to prevent neighborhood airborne spread. Use copper-based defensive sprays if cool, damp weather persists.

Potato___healthy.title: Potato: Perfectly Healthy! 🥔
Potato___healthy.advice: Strong, productive canopy. Hill your potatoes up with clean soil or mulch regularly to keep developing underground tubers completely hidden from direct sunlight.

Raspberry___healthy.title: Raspberry: Perfectly Healthy! 🍓
Raspberry___healthy.advice: Excellent cane development. Prune out floricanes (spent two-year-old woody canes) completely after harvest to channel cellular energy into next year's green primocanes.

Soybean___healthy.title: Soybean: Perfectly Healthy! 🌱
Soybean___healthy.advice: Optimal nitrogen fixation and canopy cover. Keep an eye out for early warning signs of leaf-chewing beetles or aphids as pod filling begins.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.title: Squash: Powdery Mildew 🎃
Squash___Powdery_mildew.advice: Talcum powder-like white circles blanketing squash leaves, reducing photosynthesis. Provide full sun and water only at the soil line. Spray a mixture of 1 part milk to 9 parts water in bright sunlight as an effective organic preventative.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.title: Strawberry: Leaf Scorch 🍓
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.advice: Produces purple blotches that expand until the entire leaf dries up and looks scorched. Purge older infected runner plants. Avoid overhead watering systems and apply defensive fungicides prior to spring bloom.

Strawberry___healthy.title: Strawberry: Perfectly Healthy! 🍓
Strawberry___healthy.advice: Healthy runners and crown layout. Keep fruit suspended off bare soil using clean straw mulch to block ground-dwelling gray mold spores.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.title: Tomato: Bacterial Spot 🍅
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.advice: Causes small, greasy dark spots on leaves that eventually turn yellow and drop. Disinfect gardening stakes and cages with a 10% bleach solution between seasons. Treat with a combined copper and mancozeb spray if spotted.

Tomato___Early_blight.title: Tomato: Early Blight 🍅
Tomato___Early_blight.advice: Fungal target-board spots starting on the lowest, oldest leaves. Prune off the bottom 12 inches of leaves to prevent soil-dwelling spores from splashing up during heavy rainstorms. Mulch the base heavily.

Tomato___Late_blight.title: Tomato: Late Blight 🍅
Tomato___Late_blight.advice: Large, greasy blue-gray patches on leaves that can destroy a whole tomato patch in days under humid conditions. Pull out and bag infected plants immediately. Do not compost them. Treat surrounding healthy plants with protective copper copper sulfate.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.title: Tomato: Leaf Mold 🍅
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.advice: Olive-green to gray velvety mold coating the undersides of leaves, common in enclosed greenhouses. Maximize cross-ventilation using fans and keep greenhouse relative humidity levels strictly below 85%.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.title: Tomato: Septoria Leaf Spot 🍅
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.advice: Numerous tiny circular spots with dark borders and grey centers. Spores are spread by water splash. Avoid working among wet tomato plants and apply organic bio-fungicides continuously throughout wet summer weeks.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.title: Tomato: Two-Spotted Spider Mites 🕷️
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.advice: Tiny yellow stippling dots on leaves accompanied by fine silky webbing on the undersides. Mites thrive in hot, dusty conditions. Blast the undersides of leaves with sharp bursts of clean water or apply organic insecticidal neem oil soaps.

Tomato___Target_Spot.title: Tomato: Target Spot 🍅
Tomato___Target_Spot.advice: Fungal spots with distinct concentric rings that do not look restricted by leaf veins. Improve interior airflow by aggressively removing non-productive sucker stems. Apply standard protective fungicides.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.title: Tomato: Yellow Leaf Curl Virus ⚠️
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.advice: Leaves curl dramatically upward like cups and display severe yellow edges; plant growth stunts completely. Spread exclusively by silverleaf whiteflies. Protect young crops using fine insect netting covers.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.title: Tomato: Mosaic Virus ⚠️
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.advice: Leaves display a light/dark green mottled mosaic pattern and become narrow or misshapen like fern leaves. Highly contagious via hands and tools. Wash all tools thoroughly with soap and warm water; instantly remove all infected host stock.

Tomato___healthy.title: Tomato: Perfectly Healthy! 🍅
Tomato___healthy.advice: Excellent vegetative structure. Keep pinching off non-fruiting lateral sucker stems to focus all your plant's metabolic energy into producing large, juicy tomatoes!
